intro: Hi! Today you start reading real English: menus, signs on doors, business cards and simple forms. You don't need to understand every word. Look for the words you already know, like numbers, food and colours. Warm-up: what does WELCOME mean on a hotel door?
teachingNotes: Reading at A0 means finding key words, not reading every word. Encourage learners to look for nouns, numbers and colours they already know, and to guess the rest from the place (shop door, menu, form).

Signs in scope: OPEN, CLOSED, ENTRANCE, EXIT / WAY OUT, TOILETS (US: restroom), PUSH, PULL, NO SMOKING, LIFT (US: elevator), STAFF ONLY. Learners often mix up PUSH (dorong) and PULL (tarik), and ENTRANCE (masuk) and EXIT (keluar).
Business cards: name, job title, company (PT / CV), mobile, email, address. Clues: @ means an email; 08… or +62 8… is a phone number (+62 replaces the first 0).

Forms: first name vs surname / last name / family name confuses learners because many Indonesian names have no family name. Date of birth is day/month/year in the UK and Indonesia but month/day/year in the US. BLOCK CAPITALS = huruf kapital semua.

Don't teach grammar here; answers are one word, a short phrase or a number. Learners know numbers to 20 in words; longer numbers stay as digits. Indonesian prices use a dot (Rp 15.000) where English texts often use a comma (15,000).
OPEN/CLOSED: learners met 'Close your book' (an instruction), so CLOSED on a sign looks wrong. Explain: CLOSE = the action (tutup!), CLOSED = the state (sedang tutup). OPEN is the same word for both.
Menu items reverse the Indonesian order: nasi goreng = fried rice, es teh = iced tea, mi ayam = chicken noodles. The describing word comes first in English.
British vs American on signs and cards: WAY OUT / LADIES / GENTS / LIFT / mobile are British; EXIT / RESTROOM / ELEVATOR / cell are American. Also the decimal point: 1.5 kg = 1,5 kg.
Surname with Indonesian names: the last word is often not a family name, but on English forms people usually write it under Surname anyway; one-word names: follow the form's notes or ask.

keyPoints.title: Read the key words
keyPoints.explanation: On menus, posters and notes, find the words you know first: things, numbers, colours. You can understand the message without every word.

id.title: Baca kata kuncinya
id.explanation: Di menu, poster, dan catatan, cari dulu kata yang sudah kamu tahu: nama benda, angka, warna. Kamu bisa paham pesannya tanpa harus mengerti setiap kata.

keyPoints.title: Common signs
keyPoints.explanation: Signs use one or two words, often in capitals. Learn the pairs: OPEN / CLOSED, ENTRANCE / EXIT, PUSH / PULL.

id.title: Papan tanda yang umum
id.explanation: Papan tanda memakai satu atau dua kata, sering dengan huruf kapital. Hafalkan pasangannya: OPEN / CLOSED, ENTRANCE / EXIT, PUSH / PULL.

keyPoints.title: Business cards and forms
keyPoints.explanation: A business card shows name, job title, company, phone and email. A form asks for first name, surname, date of birth, address and signature.

id.title: Kartu nama dan formulir
id.explanation: Kartu nama berisi nama, jabatan, perusahaan, nomor telepon, dan email. Formulir menanyakan nama depan (first name), nama belakang (surname), tanggal lahir, alamat, dan tanda tangan.

guidedPractice.prompt: Read the shop poster: 'Rice 5 kg · Rp 75.000'. How many kilos of rice are in the bag? Write the number.
guidedPractice.hint: Look for the number next to kg.

guidedPractice.prompt: What does the sign ENTRANCE mean in Indonesian?
A door says PUSH. Write the Indonesian word for it.
Read the card: 'Dewi Lestari · Teacher · SMA Negeri 3 Bandung · dewi.lestari@gmail.com'. What is her email?

independentPractice.prompt: Read the note: 'Lunch: rice, chicken, tea.' What is the drink?
independentPractice.hint: Which of the three do you drink?

independentPractice.prompt: A form says 'Signature: ______'. What do you do there? Answer in Indonesian or English.
independentPractice.hint: You do it with a pen at the end of the form, not with your printed name.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Read the board at a warung: 'Tea Rp 5.000 · Coffee Rp 8.000 · Water Rp 4.000'. Which drink costs Rp 8.000? Choose the word.
Choose the correct answer. Read the note on the door: 'Meeting today in Room 5.' Which room is the meeting in? Choose the number.
Choose the correct answer. Fire! You need to leave the building. Which sign do you follow: ENTRANCE, EXIT or LIFT? Choose the word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: EXIT. ENTRANCE or LIFT = 0 (you don't use the lift in a fire).

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. The sign on the pharmacy door says CLOSED. Can you buy medicine there now? Choose yes or no.
Choose the correct answer. Read the business card: 'Sari Wulandari · Marketing Manager · PT Maju Jaya · Mobile: 0812 3456 7890 · sari@majujaya.co.id'. What is Sari's job? Choose it in English.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Marketing Manager (accept 'manager'). 'PT Maju Jaya' (the company) = 0. 'Manajer pemasaran' (right meaning, Indonesian) = 70.

assessment.prompt: Read the form: 'First name: Budi · Surname: Santoso · Phone: 0857 1122 3344 · City: Bandung'. What is Budi's surname?

blocks.text: You don't need to read every word. On a menu, a poster or a note, first find the words you **already know**: things, numbers, colours. They carry most of the meaning. Big words at the top (like **Welcome** or **Menu**) tell you what the text is.

id.text: Kamu tidak perlu membaca setiap kata. Di menu, poster atau catatan, cari dulu kata yang **sudah kamu tahu**: benda, angka, warna. Kata-kata itu membawa sebagian besar artinya. Kata besar di atas (seperti **Welcome** atau **Menu**) memberi tahu teks apa itu.

rows.id: Wi-Fi gratis (free di sini = gratis; free juga bisa berarti bebas)

blocks.text: Prices: Indonesia writes **Rp 15.000** with a dot. Many English texts write **15,000** with a comma. Both mean fifteen thousand. Careful, it also works the other way: in English a dot is for a part of a number, so **1.5 kg** = 1,5 kg (satu setengah kilo).

id.text: Harga: di Indonesia ditulis **Rp 15.000** dengan titik. Banyak teks bahasa Inggris menulis **15,000** dengan koma. Keduanya artinya lima belas ribu. Hati-hati, kebalikannya juga berlaku: dalam bahasa Inggris titik dipakai untuk pecahan, jadi **1.5 kg** = 1,5 kg (satu setengah kilo).

blocks.text: On menus, the order of the words is the **opposite** of Indonesian. In English the describing word comes **first**: *nasi goreng* = **fried rice**, *es teh* = **iced tea**, *mi ayam* = **chicken noodles**. So read to the **last** word to know what the thing is: fried **rice** is rice.

id.text: Di menu, urutan katanya **kebalikan** dari bahasa Indonesia. Dalam bahasa Inggris kata yang menjelaskan ada **di depan**: *nasi goreng* = **fried rice**, *es teh* = **iced tea**, *mi ayam* = **chicken noodles**. Jadi baca sampai kata **terakhir** untuk tahu bendanya apa: fried **rice** itu nasi.

blocks.prompt: A café menu says: 'Drinks: tea, juice, water'. Which word is NOT on this list?
blocks.explain: The list has tea, juice and water. Coffee is not there.

id.explain: Daftarnya berisi tea, juice dan water. Coffee tidak ada.
id.prompt: Menu kafe bertuliskan: 'Drinks: tea, juice, water'. Kata mana yang TIDAK ada di daftar itu?

blocks.text: Signs use one or two words, often in **CAPITAL LETTERS** (huruf besar). Many come in pairs: **OPEN / CLOSED**, **ENTRANCE / EXIT**, **PUSH / PULL**. Learn them as pairs and you can read most doors in a mall, a station or an airport.

id.text: Papan tanda memakai satu atau dua kata, sering dengan **HURUF KAPITAL** (huruf besar semua). Banyak yang berpasangan: **OPEN / CLOSED**, **ENTRANCE / EXIT**, **PUSH / PULL**. Pelajari berpasangan, maka kamu bisa membaca sebagian besar pintu di mal, stasiun atau bandara.

rows.note: US: Restroom; UK also LADIES / GENTS

id.note: Amerika (US): Restroom; di Inggris (UK) juga LADIES / GENTS

blocks.text: Why **CLOSED** and not *close*? You know *Close your book*: **close** is the action (tutup! = do it now). **CLOSED** with **-ed** is the state: the shop *is* closed (sedang tutup). **OPEN** is the same word for both. Some signs are British and some American: **WAY OUT**, **LIFT** and **LADIES / GENTS** are British; **EXIT**, **ELEVATOR** and **RESTROOM** are American. You'll see both in Indonesia.

id.text: Kenapa **CLOSED**, bukan *close*? Kamu tahu *Close your book*: **close** adalah tindakannya (tutup! = lakukan sekarang). **CLOSED** dengan **-ed** adalah keadaannya: tokonya sedang tutup. **OPEN** sama untuk keduanya. Ada tanda versi Inggris (British) dan versi Amerika: **WAY OUT**, **LIFT** dan **LADIES / GENTS** versi Inggris; **EXIT**, **ELEVATOR** dan **RESTROOM** versi Amerika. Di Indonesia kamu bisa melihat keduanya.

blocks.text: Many doors in Indonesia show both languages: **PUSH / DORONG** and **PULL / TARIK**. Read the word before you touch the door!

id.text: Banyak pintu di Indonesia memakai dua bahasa: **PUSH / DORONG** dan **PULL / TARIK**. Baca kata itu sebelum kamu menyentuh pintunya!

blocks.prompt: You want to go into a building. Which sign do you look for?
blocks.explain: ENTRANCE = pintu masuk. EXIT is the way out, and STAFF ONLY is only for workers.

id.explain: ENTRANCE = pintu masuk. EXIT adalah jalan keluar, dan STAFF ONLY hanya untuk karyawan.
id.prompt: Kamu mau masuk ke sebuah gedung. Papan tanda mana yang kamu cari?

blocks.text: A business card (*kartu nama*) has one piece of information on each line: **name**, **job title**, **company**, **phone**, **email** and **address**. Use clues: **@** means an email, **08…** or **+62 8…** is a phone number, **PT** or **CV** is a company, **Jl.** starts an address.

id.text: Kartu nama berisi satu informasi di setiap baris: **name** (nama), **job title** (jabatan), **company** (perusahaan), **phone** (telepon), **email** dan **address** (alamat). Pakai petunjuk: **@** berarti email, **08…** atau **+62 8…** adalah nomor telepon, **PT** atau **CV** adalah perusahaan, **Jl.** mengawali alamat.

blocks.text: **+62** is Indonesia's country code. **+62 811 2233 4455** is the same number as **0811 2233 4455**: +62 replaces the first 0.

id.text: **+62** adalah kode negara Indonesia. **+62 811 2233 4455** sama dengan **0811 2233 4455**: +62 menggantikan angka 0 di depan.

blocks.prompt: Which line on a business card is the email?
blocks.explain: An email always has @. The numbers are a phone number, and Jl. starts an address.

id.explain: Email selalu memakai @. Deretan angka itu nomor telepon, dan Jl. mengawali alamat.
id.prompt: Baris mana di kartu nama yang merupakan email?

blocks.text: Forms at a hotel, a school or an office ask for the same things. **First name** is your own name; **surname** (also **last name** or **family name**) is the family part, usually at the end. Many Indonesian names have no family name, but on English forms people usually write the **last word** of their name next to *Surname*. **Date of birth** is your birthday with the year. **Signature** means you sign with a pen. **BLOCK CAPITALS** means write in capital letters only (huruf besar semua).

id.text: Formulir di hotel, sekolah atau kantor menanyakan hal yang sama. **First name** adalah nama depanmu; **surname** (juga **last name** atau **family name**) adalah nama keluarga, biasanya di akhir. Banyak nama Indonesia tidak punya nama keluarga, tapi di formulir berbahasa Inggris orang biasanya menulis **kata terakhir** namanya di bagian *Surname*. **Date of birth** adalah tanggal lahirmu lengkap dengan tahun. **Signature** artinya tanda tangan dengan pulpen. **BLOCK CAPITALS** artinya tulis dengan huruf kapital semua (huruf besar semua).

blocks.text: Dates: the UK and Indonesia write **day/month/year**, but the US writes **month/day/year**. On a US form, 05/06/2000 is the 6th of May. If you have only one name, read the notes on the form or ask where to write it.

id.text: Tanggal: Inggris (UK) dan Indonesia menulis **hari/bulan/tahun**, tapi Amerika Serikat menulis **bulan/hari/tahun**. Di formulir AS, 05/06/2000 artinya 6 Mei. Kalau namamu hanya satu kata, baca catatan di formulir atau tanyakan di mana menuliskannya.

blocks.prompt: Rina Wijaya fills in a form. What does she write next to 'Surname'?
blocks.explain: Surname is the family part of the name, at the end: Wijaya. Rina is her first name.

id.explain: Surname adalah nama keluarga, di bagian akhir: Wijaya. Rina adalah nama depannya.
id.prompt: Rina Wijaya mengisi formulir. Apa yang dia tulis di sebelah 'Surname'?

id.intro: Hai! Hari ini kamu mulai membaca bahasa Inggris sungguhan: menu, papan tanda di pintu, kartu nama dan formulir sederhana. Kamu tidak perlu mengerti setiap kata. Cari kata yang sudah kamu tahu, seperti angka, makanan dan warna. Pemanasan: apa arti WELCOME di pintu hotel?

assessment.read-1: Pilih jawaban yang benar. Baca papan menu di warung: 'Tea Rp 5.000 · Coffee Rp 8.000 · Water Rp 4.000'. Minuman apa yang harganya Rp 8.000? Pilih katanya dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.read-2: Pilih jawaban yang benar. Baca catatan di pintu: 'Meeting today in Room 5.' Rapatnya di ruangan nomor berapa? Pilih angkanya.
assessment.read-3: Pilih jawaban yang benar. Ada kebakaran! Kamu harus keluar dari gedung. Tanda mana yang kamu ikuti: ENTRANCE, EXIT atau LIFT? Pilih katanya.
assessment.read-4: Pilih jawaban yang benar. Tulisan di pintu apotek: CLOSED. Bisakah kamu membeli obat di sana sekarang? Pilih yes atau no.
assessment.read-5: Pilih jawaban yang benar. Baca kartu nama ini: 'Sari Wulandari · Marketing Manager · PT Maju Jaya · Mobile: 0812 3456 7890 · sari@majujaya.co.id'. Apa pekerjaan Sari? Pilih dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.read-6: Baca formulir ini: 'First name: Budi · Surname: Santoso · Phone: 0857 1122 3344 · City: Bandung'. Apa nama belakang (surname) Budi?
